raw_response: This bar chart displays the mean effect sizes for six different language model architectures—mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂—across nine linguistic categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The horizontal axis lists these linguistic categories in order from left to right, while the vertical axis represents the “effect” on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 30. Each category contains six colored bars, each corresponding to one of the six model architectures as indicated in the legend: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). Error bars extend vertically from each bar, indicating the standard error of the mean. The heights of the bars vary significantly across categories and models; for example, in the IE-Indic category, the mBERT-B₂ (light pink) and XLM-B₂ (dark red) bars are the tallest, reaching approximately 23 and 21 respectively, while in the Isolate category, all bars are very short, with values near zero. In the Semitic category, the XLM-B₂ (dark red) bar is the tallest, reaching approximately 20, while the mBERT-R₂ (dark green) bar is the shortest, near zero. The bars are not sorted by height; they are presented in the order of the linguistic categories as listed on the x-axis. No bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding and error bars.
